title: Golden-sample selection and publish orchestration for verified performance profiles
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: As the performance catalog grows we need deterministic, low-variance performance profiles that reflect multi-regional production traffic while minimizing lab measurement noise. Current publish runs produce inconsistent latency tails across regions and make pinning brittle for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Goal: Define a reproducible 'golden sample' selection algorithm and an automated publish orchestration that: (1) selects representative input traces, (2) runs deterministic profiling across regions and model variants, (3) applies cost-normalization and quantile-based gating, and (4) publishes a signed, provenance-traceable verified profile with rollback metadata. This should reduce flaky pin rollbacks and accelerate safe model onboarding for runtime and Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Golden-sample algorithm defined and documented (confluence) with deterministic seeding and sampling weights for region/tenant strata
Profiling harness integrated with nightly job runner and supports reruns with identical seeds to reproduce results
Publish orchestration enforces gating rules: 95th latency < gated-threshold AND cost-per-k-token within expected bounds OR profile is flagged for manual review
Published profiles include metadata fields: seed-id, dataset-hash, region-weights, profiling-image-hash, git-commit, signed-by, and expiry/decay policy
Rollback metadata and lightweight diff exposed in profile catalog UI and CLI for stewards
End-to-end test that exercises failure mode: synthetic traffic skew to a single region -> publish should be blocked and a ticket auto-created
steps: Prototype golden-sample selector: implement stratified sampling of production traces with portable seed generation
Extend profiling harness to accept seed and sample manifest; add deterministic RNG and store sample manifest artifact
Build publish-orchestration lambda that fetches run artifacts, normalizes cost across instance types and regions, computes quantiles, and evaluates gates
Wire signature/provenance step: sign artifact with steward key and emit registry entry to git-backed ledger
Add UI affordances: profile detail page shows provenance, compare-to-current pin, and one-click rollback
Add automation: scheduled reverify (auto-refresh) and archival/decay policy for stale profiles
updates: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff sync: aligned with Runtime Eng, Observability, and Console. Agreed to prototype in staging with 3region sample (us-west1, eu-west1, ap-south1). Action: ENG to provide small traffic trace samples.
2026-03-05 — Design review: proposed sample manifest format (CSV with trace-id, timestamp, weight, region). Observability suggested adding user-agent and seq-len bucketing. Luca to update spec.

2026-03-08 — Trade-off discussion: deterministic seeding increases reproducibility but may underrepresent rare tails. Decided to include an 'exploration bucket' in manifest for tail sampling. Logged rationale in confluence: /confluence/redwood/perf-profiles/golden-sample

2026-03-10 — Prototype ready: harness accepts --seed and --manifest. Initial runs show 8% reduction in median variance across three independent runs. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/4821 (profiling harness)

2026-03-12 — Gating rules draft: use 95th latency and cost-per-1k-tokens quantiles; require both to be within +/-10% of staging anchors OR require manual steward approval. PM/Eng to validate thresholds on historical data. Link to dashboard: grafana.redwood.com/d/PerfProfiles/cluster-comparison

2026-03-13 — Security reviewed signature approach; SSO/KMS integration required for steward keys. Security asked for an HSM-backed key-rotation plan. Added security_review_required flag. Action: Security to propose KMS flow by 2026-03-20

2026-03-14 — Canary publish plan drafted: 0.5% shadow traffic -> 5% routed with canary pin -> 25% -> full. Console will show decay timer and provenance. Next: ENG to implement publish lambda and UI mocks. Design follow-up scheduled.
review_feedback: Observability: request to include bootstrapped sample variance in profile metadata so consumers can understand expected instability
Runtime Eng: prefer cost-normalization using VM-equivalent token rate instead of raw instance-hour cost to reflect throughput differences
Design: profile detail should highlight 'why this profile was published' with a short human summary and links to raw run artifacts
Security: steward signing must be auditable; prefer git-backed ledger with signed commit and KMS key reference
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting to sampled traces -> mitigation: holdout set + periodic blind reverify against recent production traces
Risk: Publish pipeline stalls due to transient infra flakiness -> mitigation: retry policy, deterministic rerun with same seed and manifest, and auto-create incident ticket if >3 retries
Risk: Cost-normalization mismatch across cloud providers -> mitigation: normalize to throughput-equivalent tokens and maintain provider conversion table
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): run nightly for all incoming candidate models and store artifacts (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (shadow): run publish orchestration in dry-run against the live catalog and compare decisions (1 week)
Phase 3 (canary): enable signed publish for non-critical models with 0.5% shadow traffic and manual steward approval to advance
Phase 4 (GA): automated publish for low-risk models with signed provenance and scheduled reverify every 14 days
